text:
Follow-up: the cadence work exposed a worse adjacent defect. Every poll aborted the entire await on a single failed round trip -- readResult AgentCall.Failed, and accounting AgentCall.Failed / InvocationFailed / ParseFailed all returned terminally. Across a long wait a lost SSH round trip is close to certain, so a 24 h await could be discarded at hour 19 by one hiccup that said nothing about the job.

RemoteAwaitPolicy gains maximumConsecutiveObservationFailures (default 5). Both poll loops now ride out transient blindness and reset the count on any successful observation; only a persistent run surrenders, and it reports the observation failure itself rather than a timeout. terminalAccounting was also conflating 'accounting says this job died' with 'accounting could not be read' -- it now returns a three-way AccountingProbe (Terminal / Unavailable / Inconclusive), so an unreadable sacct response is tolerated instead of ending the wait. That is also what makes the stricter accounting parser in P6f.32 safe to ship.

Evidence: two new RemoteTaskSuite tests using a FlakySshRunner that injects transport failures on demand -- a wait rides out 2 injected failures and still returns 42, and a wait under persistent failure surrenders after exactly the configured bound. ssh 31/31; full gate green (289 tests, mima, doc).
